newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire ex-envoy to stand trial in France in March.
newsitem.headline: Zaire ex-envoy to stand trial in France in March.

text.p: Zaire's former ambassador to Paris will stand trial in France on March 25 for aggravated manslaughter, over the deaths of two boys in a traffic accident on the French Riviera, justice sources said on Wednesday.

They said ex-envoy Ramazani Baya, who returned to France at the weekend without diplomatic immunity, was ordered to face a court in Nice on charges of manslaughter aggravated by unsafe and careless conduct.
The charge carries a penalty of up to three years in prison.

Baya was on his way to visit President Mobutu Sese Seko, recuperating from cancer therapy at his Riviera villa, when he hit Raphael Lenoir, 13, and Ronald Lehartel, 12, on a pedestrian crossing in the Mediterranean resort of Menton last November.
Police have said he was driving at more than twice the legal speed limit.
Mobutu said Baya had been relieved of his ambassadorial duties but Baya himself said he had resigned so he could face a court in France and clear his conscience.
Relatives and neighbours of the two boys had demonstrated to demand that he be brought to justice, and the French government had asked Zaire to lift his diplomatic immunity so he could face justice.
